author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory narrows to one specialty on both surfaces
summary: A reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to a single specialty on the page surface and on the machine-readable surface. Without a specialty both surfaces behave exactly as today.
acceptance_criteria: The page surface at /vets.html accepts an optional specialty value and lists only veterinarians holding that specialty.
The machine-readable surface at /vets accepts the same optional specialty value and carries only those veterinarians.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case; the opening letters of a name match nothing.
Surrounding spaces on the value are disregarded before matching, following the owner-search convention.
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields the normal page or document with an empty veterinarian list and a success response, not an error.
An empty or blank value behaves as if no specialty were given, the same convention as the empty owner search.
With no specialty value, both surfaces behave exactly as they do today.
Paging applies to the narrowed list, and the links that move between pages carry the specialty value.
Automated tests cover each outcome above on the surface it names.
non_goals: A form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing a specialty; the narrowing is asked for in the request only
Free-text search over veterinarians, which NG-9 still bars
Prefix or partial matching on a specialty name
Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2)
Narrowing any list other than the veterinarian directory
notes: Slice delivers both requirements together: REQ-VET-001 gains the narrowing on the page surface and REQ-VET-003 is the fresh requirement for the machine-readable surface, minted 2026-08-25. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. NG-9 was narrowed to free-text search only; see docs/adr/2026-08-25-non-goal-vet-directory-filtering.md. That ADR still needs an index row in docs/adr/README.md, which is outside the product-requirements-expert write scope. Two open questions are recorded in the PRD: whether a visible control should follow, and confirmation that surrounding spaces on the value are meant to be disregarded.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the vet feature package with its first query-level narrowing and reinstates the machine-readable route as a supported surface. It follows the owner-search shape (paged, filtered, normalized in the controller) but must not follow its case-sensitivity, which is a recorded defect. Filtering belongs in the repository query so paging applies to the narrowed list; the controller normalizes and chooses between the filtered and unfiltered finder; the template carries the value on every pagination link. docs/system-design.md gained a 'The veterinarian directory's narrowing' paragraph under Contracts, updated vet Contracts rows, an amended Overview, a new Security Context input, and two Threat Model rows; the stale Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route 'pending removal' was removed. One ADR records the matching strategy.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two declarative finders mirroring the existing findAll pair: Page<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) for the HTML route and Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) for the JSON route. Both carry @Transactional(readOnly = true). Neither carries @Cacheable.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each gain @RequestParam(defaultValue = "") String specialty; each strips the value and calls the unfiltered finder when the result is empty, so the no-parameter path stays byte-identical to today including its cache entry.
addPaginationModel puts the normalized specialty into the model so the template can carry it; the JSON route needs no model change.
vetList.html rewrites its five pagination links from the string-preprocessing form @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} to the named-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}.
docs/system-design.md Contracts now maps VetRepository, VetController, and Vets to REQ-VET-003 alongside REQ-VET-001.

patterns.description: the normalization convention to mirror: strip the value, treat the empty result as the broadest read, then choose the finder. The vet routes use defaultValue = "" rather than the null dance, so strip() is null-safe.
the existing findAll()/findAll(Pageable) pair the two new finders mirror in shape, transaction annotation, and javadoc style.

the @DataJpaTest home for the matching tests. Real H2 with the seeded specialties radiology, surgery, dentistry — the only place case-insensitivity, prefix-non-match, and the empty result can actually be proven.

risks.risk: Relying on the database collation for case-insensitivity repeats the REQ-OWN-002 defect exactly. specialties.name is VARCHAR(80) on H2, TEXT on PostgreSQL, and default-collated VARCHAR(80) on MySQL, so a plain findBySpecialtiesName matches case-insensitively on MySQL alone.
risks.mitigation: The IgnoreCase keyword on the derived finder, which emits upper(name) = upper(?) on every vendor. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-25-case-insensitive-specialty-matching.md.

risks.risk: Annotating the new finders @Cacheable("vets") would key cache entries on a caller-supplied string. The vets JCache configures no size limit and every route is unauthenticated, so a caller could grow it without bound.
risks.mitigation: The narrowed finders carry no cache annotation. Recorded as a Threat Model row in docs/system-design.md.

risks.risk: Concatenating the specialty into the existing @{'...__${...}__'} link form would put unencoded caller input into every href.
risks.mitigation: The named-parameter link form URL-encodes the value. If Thymeleaf renders a bare specialty= for a blank value, behavior is unchanged since blank is treated as absent; putting null in the model when blank is the alternative if the rendered link must match today's byte for byte.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is an EAGER @ManyToMany. A derived finder that joins the collection under a Pageable can trip Hibernate's in-memory pagination (HHH000104) if the collection is fetch-joined.
risks.mitigation: Keep the finder declarative with no explicit fetch join, and assert getTotalElements and getTotalPages in the @DataJpaTest against seeded data rather than only the content list.

risks.risk: VetControllerTests stubs VetRepository with @MockitoBean, so no assertion there can prove the matching semantics — a stub returns whatever it is told regardless of letter case.
risks.mitigation: Split the coverage: the matching criteria (case, prefix, no-match) go to ClinicServiceTests against real H2; VetControllerTests covers parameter binding, the blank-equals-absent branch, the model attribute, and the pagination links. testing-principles § Mocking Policy asks new tests to reach for real implementations first.

risks.risk: Owner list pagination drops the lastName today, so copying that template wholesale would drop the specialty and fail an explicit acceptance criterion.
risks.mitigation: Do not copy ownersList.html. theVetDirectoryPagingShouldKeepTheRequestedSpecialty is the test that pins it; the seeded directory holds six vets against a page size of five, so a narrowed multi-page case needs its own fixture rather than the seed.

risks.risk: Paging the whole directory and filtering the page in the controller would produce short pages and wrong totals.
risks.mitigation: The narrowing is applied by the query. The page count assertion in the @DataJpaTest catches the mistake.

notes: Housekeeping, both done: docs/adr/README.md gained index rows for the non-goal ADR and for the new matching ADR; the non-goal ADR conformed to the template except for its missing References heading, which was added over its existing links (its Implementation section correctly uses **Non-goal:** NG-9). Reinstatement is now reflected everywhere — the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route 'pending removal' was deleted, the Overview no longer claims the app has no JSON surface, and the vet Contracts rows carry REQ-VET-003. A repository-wide grep for 'pending removal', 'deprecated', and 'REQ-VET-002' outside docs/prd.md now returns only the ADR template's status enum. Open questions taken at their narrowest reading rather than escalated: the strip convention is applied as the PRD reads it (PRD Open Questions records the confirmation still pending); no page control is added; the blank value routes to the existing cached finder. The owner-search case-sensitivity defect is NOT repaired here — the new ADR names the pattern a future repair can follow. No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit. Procedural note against my own contract: the dispatch-start record landed at line 3 after two orienting reads rather than as the first tool call.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: checkFormat passes clean (task is named checkFormat, not checkJavaFormat, in this project's build.gradle)
normalize()'s javadoc claim of following the owner-search blank-is-absent convention checked out against OwnerController.java:98-103

Naming, method length, and control flow all follow the existing codebase's conventions with no new violations introduced

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the specialty narrowing uses the Spring Data derived finder findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) — the caller value is bound as a JPA query parameter, never concatenated into JPQL or native SQL. No @Query, no EntityManager string building, no Criteria literal anywhere in the diff. No SQL-injection exposure.

Cache decision held as designed: @Cacheable("vets") remains on both unfiltered finders (VetRepository findAll() and findAll(Pageable)); neither filtered finder carries it, and the omission is documented in the Javadoc. The unbounded 'vets' cache (CacheConfiguration.java:37, no size limit) is therefore never keyed on caller-supplied text arriving on an unauthenticated route.

Reflected XSS: swept every branch of vetList.html. All eight pagination hrefs use the named-parameter form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}; no '__${...}__' preprocessing remains in the file (grep -F '__${' matches only the warning comment at line 29). Thymeleaf URL-encodes the parameter value and HTML-escapes the attribute, so '&', '=', '"' and '<' cannot break out of the href. The value reaches the page through no other sink — no th:text, th:utext, th:attr or inlining of ${specialty} exists in the template, and grep -F 'th:utext' finds none anywhere under templates/. Encoding is regression-covered by theVetDirectoryPagingShouldUrlEncodeTheRequestedSpecialty.
Parameter-splitting / open-redirect: the encoded value cannot inject an extra query parameter, and the link path is a fixed literal, so no attacker-controlled destination.

JSON surface: /vets returns the unchanged Vets/Vet/Specialty shape (id, first name, last name, specialty names). The reinstated filter narrows the result set; it adds no field and widens no projection, so it introduces no new data exposure. Vet names are already public directory data under the system-design threat model.
Blank/whitespace handling is a strip() on a String parameter — no path, file, command, deserialization or reflection sink is reached by the caller value on either route.

Secrets: swept the added lines for password/secret/token/api-key/credential/private-key/Authorization. The only hit is prose in docs/system-design.md restating that datasource credentials come from environment variables. No credential material introduced.
Supply chain: build.gradle, settings.gradle and gradle/ are untouched by the change set, so the dependency graph and its CVE surface are unchanged by this slice.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: vetList.html carries five pagination links (numbered pages, first, previous, next, last), each with its own filtered/unfiltered ternary. Every paging test in VetControllerTests that supplies a specialty (theVetDirectoryPagingShouldKeepTheRequestedSpecialty, theVetDirectoryPagingShouldUrlEncodeTheRequestedSpecialty) requests page=1 of a 2-page result, so currentPage>1 is always false and the 'first' and 'previous' anchors never render (th:if="${currentPage > 1}").
